ablation_plan: Replace alternating half-cell row offsets with aligned rows while preserving the same normalization and evaluator path.
Replace the triangular-lattice constructor with its inherited SEED constructor while preserving all controls.
assumptions: The frozen evaluator computes the stated squared minimum-to-maximum pairwise-distance ratio from the returned coordinates.
A staggered triangular-lattice arrangement can increase nearest-neighbor separation relative to its diameter for 16 points.
The editable function may construct and normalize a fixed deterministic coordinate array without modifying the evaluator.
failure_risks: Boundary rows may determine the diameter without contributing enough nearest-neighbor separation.
The finite 16-point truncation may negate the packing advantage of the triangular lattice.
An implementation error could violate the exact 16-by-2 shape or finite-value requirement.
candidate.falsifier: Falsify the mechanism if the frozen upstream evaluator completes on the deterministic finite 16-by-2 candidate but min_max_ratio is not strictly greater than the frozen public baseline result, or if repeated evaluations produce different coordinates or scores.
candidate.hypothesis: Replacing the inherited point constructor with a fixed, diameter-normalized 4-by-4 staggered triangular lattice will improve the minimum pairwise separation relative to the configuration diameter because alternating row offsets give interior points six-directional packing geometry rather than axis-aligned neighborhood geometry.
candidate.intervention: In experiments/engine_bakeoff/minmax16/initial.py, change min_max_dist_dim2_16 to construct four rows of four points with alternating half-spacing horizontal offsets and triangular-lattice vertical spacing, then deterministically translate and uniformly scale the complete set by its maximum pairwise distance before returning the 16-by-2 NumPy array.
mechanism_claims: Alternating half-spacing row offsets change the pairwise-distance graph from an aligned grid to a triangular-lattice packing graph.
Uniform diameter normalization preserves all pairwise-distance ratios while fixing the global scale.
The proposed constructor is deterministic and does not require fitted parameters or evaluator feedback.
